title: Why You Avoid Looking at Your Own Money
title_ru: Почему ты не хочешь смотреть на свои деньги

shots.name: mm_ep04_01_the_message_arrives
shots.vo: The message arrives while you are doing something else. Your bank, a card, a subscription you had forgotten about. You see the first line of it, and your thumb moves before you have finished reading.

shots.name: mm_ep04_02_nothing_changed_but_knowing
shots.vo: Nothing about your money changed in that second. The balance is exactly what it was a moment earlier. The only thing that changed is how much of it you know, and that changed for one person.

shots.name: mm_ep04_03_later_becomes_a_habit
shots.vo: You tell yourself you will look at it properly later, when there is time and a clearer head. For a lot of people, later stops being a plan and quietly turns into a habit.

shots.name: mm_ep04_04_not_laziness
shots.vo: Most advice treats this as laziness or weak discipline, and then offers a spreadsheet. It usually is not laziness. Avoiding your own numbers is often something your mind does actively, and it does it to protect you.

shots.name: mm_ep04_05_the_ostrich_effect
shots.vo: Researchers have described one version of this as the ostrich effect. People check their accounts less often during the periods when they expect the news to be bad, and more often when they expect it to be good.

shots.name: mm_ep04_06_face_down_statement
shots.vo: It was noticed first in investors who stopped logging in while markets were falling. The same avoidance can attach to a banking app, an unopened envelope, or a statement that stays face down on the table.

shots.name: mm_ep04_07_looking_adds_the_feeling
shots.vo: The logic underneath is quiet and almost reasonable. If looking cannot change the number, then looking only adds the feeling, and the feeling is the part that actually hurts.

shots.name: mm_ep04_08_not_knowing_feels_like_not_losing
shots.vo: So the mind begins to treat the information as though it were the event itself. Not knowing can feel a great deal like not losing, at least for the length of an afternoon.

shots.name: mm_ep04_09_not_all_information_equally
shots.vo: People do not avoid every kind of information equally. The pattern tends to be strongest around information that feels like it will say something about you, rather than merely about a situation.

shots.name: mm_ep04_10_the_number_keeps_moving
shots.vo: The difficulty is that the number keeps moving whether or not anyone is watching it. Attention is the only part of this that you switched off.

shots.name: mm_ep04_11_relief_is_instant
shots.vo: Avoidance also pays immediately. The relief is instant, it is small, and at the moment you choose it, it appears to be completely free.

shots.name: mm_ep04_12_the_cost_arrives_in_pieces
shots.vo: The cost arrives later and in pieces, each one small enough that none of them feels like the consequence of a decision you made.

shots.name: mm_ep04_13_a_quiet_tuesday
shots.vo: A subscription renews for another year. A fee lands on an account nobody was watching. A payment date passes on a quiet Tuesday.

shots.name: mm_ep04_14_nobody_collected_it
shots.vo: None of that happened because the money was missing. It happened because the information was available and no one collected it.

shots.name: mm_ep04_15_they_arrive_together
shots.vo: And by the time those pieces are visible, they usually arrive together, inside a single statement that appears to prove the exact thing you were afraid of in the first place.

shots.name: mm_ep04_16_you_still_carry_a_number
shots.vo: There is a second cost that is harder to see. When you stop checking, you do not stop carrying a number in your head.

shots.name: mm_ep04_17_the_estimate_is_worse
shots.vo: You simply replace the real one with an estimate. And the estimate is built by the part of you that is worried, which means it is almost always worse than the truth.

shots.name: mm_ep04_18_anxiety_is_a_poor_accountant
shots.vo: Anxiety is a poor accountant. It rounds in the wrong direction, it counts the same worry twice, and it never files anything away as finished.

shots.name: mm_ep04_19_a_balance_arrives_as_a_report_card
shots.vo: It helps to notice that very little of this is about arithmetic. A balance is a fact, but it rarely arrives feeling like one. It arrives feeling like a report card with your name on it.

shots.name: mm_ep04_20_the_drift
shots.vo: So the longer the gap between one look and the next, the further the imagined number drifts from the real one.

shots.name: mm_ep04_21_preparing_to_look
shots.vo: And the further it drifts, the more the next look feels like something you would need to prepare for, set aside an evening for, be ready for.

shots.name: mm_ep04_22_the_loop
shots.vo: That is the loop. Avoidance protects the feeling, the feeling grows in the dark, and the grown feeling makes the following look more expensive than the one you already skipped.

shots.name: mm_ep04_23_scarcity_narrows_attention
shots.vo: Money stress may also narrow attention in ways that make all of this harder. Research on scarcity suggests that financial worry can occupy mental bandwidth that other decisions were relying on.

shots.name: mm_ep04_24_held_lightly
shots.vo: That is one explanation rather than a settled account of every case, and it is worth holding lightly. It is offered here as a description, not a diagnosis.

shots.name: mm_ep04_25_make_looking_cheaper
shots.vo: But it does point at something useful. If avoidance is a response to cost, then the way out is probably not more discipline. It is making the act of looking cost less.

shots.name: mm_ep04_26_looking_is_not_fixing
shots.vo: Start by separating two things that almost always arrive together. Looking is not the same as fixing, even though they usually turn up in the same ten minutes.

shots.name: mm_ep04_27_opening_feels_like_agreeing
shots.vo: Most people avoid opening the app because opening it feels like agreeing, in advance, to solve everything they might find inside it.

shots.name: mm_ep04_28_a_check_with_no_decisions
shots.vo: So give looking a job of its own. A short scheduled check, with no decisions attached to it, and nothing that has to be repaired while you are in there.

shots.name: mm_ep04_29_make_it_small
shots.vo: Make the first one small enough to be unimpressive. One account. Two minutes. A timer, if a timer is what lets you leave.

shots.name: mm_ep04_30_checking_constantly_is_not_it
shots.vo: The opposite habit is not the answer either. Checking constantly can become its own kind of anxiety, where the number is watched all day and somehow still never trusted.

shots.name: mm_ep04_31_survive_a_bad_week
shots.vo: Put it somewhere in the week that can survive a bad week. The same day, the same time, ideally attached to something ordinary you already do without deciding.

shots.name: mm_ep04_32_write_down_what_you_saw
shots.vo: Write down what you actually saw. On paper, a number stops behaving like a verdict and goes back to being what it always was, which is information.

shots.name: mm_ep04_33_a_separate_appointment
shots.vo: Some of what you find will genuinely need action. That is a separate appointment with a separate feeling, and it is far easier to keep when it starts from a real number instead of an imagined one.

shots.name: mm_ep04_34_the_gap_narrows
shots.vo: After a few weeks of small checks, something quiet happens. The distance between the number you imagine and the number that is actually there stops being wide enough to frighten anyone.

shots.name: mm_ep04_35_an_estimate_built_by_worry
shots.vo: You are not behind because you have not been looking. You have been carrying an estimate assembled by worry rather than by arithmetic, and carrying it is heavier than checking it.

shots.name: mm_ep04_36_the_gap_was_the_thing
shots.vo: That distance was the thing you were avoiding. Not the balance itself, but the space between what you knew and what you feared, which only ever grows while nobody measures it.

shots.name: mm_ep04_37_look_once_on_purpose
shots.vo: Look once, briefly, on purpose. The number is usually smaller than the dread that has been standing in front of it.
